answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Each submission hangs on the plume of a task receipt, and the zenith is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, quorum must span unrelated subnetworks. What survives to the spiral is a record of labour, not a list of addresses.
